svg.title: TB-500 vs thymosin beta-4: the paper trail
svg.desc: 1966: Goldstein and White extract 'thymosin' from calf thymus; 1981: Thymosin beta-4 sequenced: 43 amino acids, studied as a thymus hormone; 1991: It turns out to be the main actin-binding peptide inside cells; 1999: NIH: full thymosin beta-4 speeds skin wound healing in rats; 2003: NIH: its 7-amino-acid actin-binding piece matches it in dish tests; 2010: Full protein: IV safety study (40 people), venous ulcer gel (73); 2011: 'TB-500' sold as a veterinary product for racehorses and greyhounds; 2012: Doping labs identify Ac-LKKTETQ in TB-500; first detection in horses; 2016: Sport court bans 34 Essendon footballers for thymosin beta-4; 2018-21: Full-protein eye drops miss primary goals in two Phase 3 dry-eye trials; 2024: TB-500 itself doesn't close scratch wounds in cells; one fragment does; 2025: Recombinant full protein, 96 heart-attack patients: no overall infarct-size difference; 2026: Only TB-500 trial record calls itself 'fictional'; FDA advisers back it

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: TB-500 vs thymosin beta-4: the paper trail

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Full protein = 43 amino acids. TB-500 = acetylated amino acids 17-23 (Ac-LKKTETQ).
